SALES CADENCE BUILDER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED OR SENT

A prospecting cadence for every lead on your list, checked before you send

Paste the prospect list you already have and describe what you sell in a few lines. You get a dated plan of emails, calls with a voicemail script, LinkedIn connection notes and mailed letters on business days, every call placed inside the prospect's own business hours, a draft for every touch, and a CSV task list and calendar file for your CRM or calendar.

Before anything is planned, each prospect is checked against your suppression list, your do-not-contact column and duplicates, and email is held back where Canadian, EU or UK rules want consent first. Every email carries your postal address and an opt-out. Want the method? Read the B2B sales cadence template.

1. You and your offer

Without a real result, the "proof" email becomes a polite ask for the right person instead. The tool never invents a customer or a number.

2. The cadence

3. Your prospects

Fill in your details and paste prospects, then click Build the cadence.

4. The plan

Who is in, and what was held back

RowProspectStatusNotes

Touches by day

Call windows are in your time zone and keep to 9:00–17:00 in the prospect's. Each draft is yours to read and edit before you send it from your own mailbox, phone or post.

Optional: personalise emails with AI, on your own key

Off by default. With a key, the "Personalise with AI" button on an email sends only that prospect's name, title, company and trigger, your offer fields and the draft, straight from this browser to the provider you pick, never to us. The model draft must pass the same checks, and may not state any number that is not in your own inputs; otherwise the template draft is kept and you are told. Your address and opt-out line are always added by the tool, not the model. The key is kept only in this browser if you tick the box.

To keep everything on your own computer, run a model locally with Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp and pick it below: no key, no cost per use. The local server must allow this page: start Ollama with OLLAMA_ORIGINS=https://duncan-haywood.github.io.

Questions

What is a sales cadence?

A sales cadence is the planned order of touches you make with one prospect: which day you email, call, connect on LinkedIn or send a letter, and what each touch says. A typical B2B cadence is six to ten touches over two to four weeks, mixing channels, and ending with a short note that says you will stop.

Does this tool send emails or make calls for me?

No. It plans and drafts; you send. You get a dated task list, a calendar file and a draft for every touch, and you send each email from your own mailbox, place each call yourself and post each letter. That keeps you in control of every message and inside the sending rules of your email provider and LinkedIn.

When is it legal to make a sales call?

In the United States the federal TCPA rule allows telephone solicitation between 8am and 9pm in the called person's local time, and some states, such as Florida, Oklahoma and Maryland, narrow that to 8am to 8pm. This tool schedules calls only between 9am and 5pm in the prospect's own time zone, shown in yours, and uses the overlap for a state that spans two time zones. Consumer numbers must also be checked against the Do Not Call registry.

Why did it drop the emails for some prospects?

Canada's anti-spam law (CASL) needs express or implied consent before commercial email, several EU countries such as Germany require consent even for business email, and in the UK a personal address counts as an individual who must opt in. Without a consent value in your list those prospects keep their calls, letters and LinkedIn note but no email. Add the basis in a consent column and run it again.

What does every cold email need?

Under CAN-SPAM a commercial email needs an honest subject line, a sender you can identify, your valid postal address and a clear way to opt out that you honour. The tool appends your name, address and an opt-out line to every email and blocks a draft whose subject pretends to be a reply.

Is Sales Cadence Builder free?

Yes. There is no signup, no limit and no seat price. It runs in your browser, so your prospect list is never uploaded, and it is MIT-licensed open source you can host yourself or run from the command line.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal or sales-compliance advice: its checks are simple rules that can be wrong for your situation, jurisdiction or list, and time-zone guesses from a state or country can be off. You are responsible for every message and call you make, including CAN-SPAM, TCPA and Do Not Call rules, CASL, GDPR and PECR, LinkedIn's terms, honouring every opt-out, and having the right to contact everyone on your list. Use only lists you are allowed to use.

Independent. Not affiliated with Outreach, Salesloft, Apollo, HubSpot, LinkedIn or any sales vendor, and none is endorsed here. The example people and companies are invented.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record: download the CSV and calendar.

Everything runs in your browser. Your prospect list and drafts are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (plan_built, example_loaded, csv_downloaded, ics_downloaded, draft_copied, ai_personalised) are counted in this browser's local storage only and can be turned off.

Related tools: the ICP lens for choosing who goes on the list, email authentication check for SPF, DKIM and DMARC before you send, the sales call notes desk for after the call is booked, and the lead response time analyzer for inbound leads.

Free and open source. If this helped, the code is under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional and never changes what the tool does.

sales-cadence-template.html.text:
Sales Cadence Builder · guide

B2B sales cadence template: 8 touches over 15 business days

A sales cadence is the order of touches you make with one prospect before you stop. This one mixes four channels, because people answer different ones: email, phone (with a voicemail when they do not pick up), a LinkedIn connection note and a mailed letter. Every touch is on a business day, every call is inside the prospect's own business hours, and the last email says you will stop, and you do.

To build it for your own list with your own words, paste the list into the Sales Cadence Builder. It does the dates, the time zones and the checks, and gives you a CSV task list and a calendar file.

The eight steps

Worked for an example prospect, starting Monday 2026-10-26.

Business dayDateChannelWhat it does
12026-10-26EmailWho you are, why them, why now, one easy question.
12026-10-26LinkedInA short note with no pitch, so your name is familiar.
32026-10-28CallOpener, one question, one ask; a 30-second voicemail if they do not pick up.
52026-10-30EmailA question about how they handle the problem today, not a pitch.
82026-11-04CallOpener, one question, one ask; a 30-second voicemail if they do not pick up.
102026-11-06LetterA one-page letter by post: few sellers send them, so it stands out.
122026-11-10EmailOne real result from a similar customer, or, with none to show, ask who owns the problem.
152026-11-13EmailSay you will stop, and stop.

Step 1: the first email

Short, specific and honest. Say why you are writing to this person now (the trigger), what you do in one sentence, and ask one question that is easy to answer. Your postal address and an opt-out line go at the bottom of every cold email; CAN-SPAM requires both.

Subject: Route planning at Brightline Logistics

Hi Dana,

I saw you opened a second depot in Aurora, so this seemed like a good time to write.

I'm Sam Ortiz at RouteLoop. RouteLoop plans delivery routes for regional fleets. We help teams spend less time building routes by hand.

Is route planning something you're working on this quarter? If it is, would a 15-minute call next week be useful?

Thanks,
Sam Ortiz

--
Sam Ortiz, RouteLoop
500 Main Street, Suite 210, Boulder, CO 80302
Not the right person, or rather not hear from me? Reply "no thanks" and I won't email you again.

The call script and voicemail

Ask for permission to talk, ask one question about how they handle the problem today, and make one ask. If they do not pick up, leave a voicemail of about thirty seconds and say your number twice. For this prospect in Colorado, the builder schedules the first call for 2026-10-28 between 09:00–17:00 Denver time, inside 9:00 to 17:00 where they are.

Opener: Hi Dana, this is Sam Ortiz from RouteLoop. I'm calling about route planning. Do you have half a minute, or is now a bad time?
Why them: I saw you opened a second depot in Aurora. RouteLoop plans delivery routes for regional fleets.
Question: How are you handling route planning today?
Ask: If it's worth a look, would a 15-minute call next week work?
If not now: ask who owns route planning or when to check back, and log the answer.
Voicemail: Hi Dana, it's Sam Ortiz from RouteLoop, calling about route planning at Brightline Logistics. We help teams spend less time building routes by hand. I'll send a short email as well. You can reach me on (720) 555-0188. Again, that's Sam Ortiz, (720) 555-0188.

Rules that apply to every cadence

  • Remove people first. Take out anyone on your suppression list or marked do-not-contact, and duplicates, before you plan a single touch. In the example, 2 of 7 rows are left out for exactly these reasons.
  • Email needs a lawful basis outside the US. Canada's CASL needs consent for commercial email, several EU countries need consent even for business email, and in the UK a personal address counts as an individual. Those prospects still get calls, letters and a LinkedIn note.
  • Call in their hours, not yours. The US federal limit is 8am to 9pm in the called person's time and some states end at 8pm; 9am to 5pm their time keeps you inside all of them and inside their working day.
  • No invented proof. If you have no real result from a similar customer, ask who owns the problem instead. Never write a number or a customer name you cannot show.

Questions

How many touches should a sales cadence have?

Most B2B cadences use six to ten touches over two to four weeks. Fewer than five gives up before a busy person has seen you; more than about twelve starts to feel like pressure. The template here uses eight touches over fifteen business days and then stops.

How long should I wait between sales follow-ups?

Two to three business days between early touches and three to four between later ones. Spacing that widens over time reads as persistent rather than pushy, and keeping touches on business days means they arrive when people work.

Which channels should a cadence mix?

Email, phone and one social or physical touch. Email is cheap and easy to reply to, a call gets a decision in one conversation, a LinkedIn connection makes your name familiar, and a mailed letter stands out because so few sellers send one.

What should the last email in a cadence say?

That you will stop, and then stop. Say you will assume the problem is not a priority, that you will not follow up again, and that they can reply if that changes. It is honest, it respects their time, and it gives a busy person an easy moment to answer.

No warranty. A template and a worked example, not legal or sales-compliance advice. You are responsible for every message and call you make and for the rules where you and your prospects are. The example people and companies are invented.

Free and open source under an MIT licence — support is entirely optional.
